atomic_propositions: The guideline provides practical guidance to ensure safe and secure packaging and transportation of clinical specimens and infectious substances within the country and abroad.
To determine appropriate packaging for transport, specimens need to be classified according to the guide as in Appendix 1.
Basic triple packaging can be used to transport clinical specimens by all modes of transportation.
Additional requirements apply to transporting infectious specimens or substances classified under Category A or Category B to ensure safe containment in various modes of transport.
Specimens should be marked and labelled adequately to convey essential information, including content of package, nature of the hazard, and the packaging standards applied.
exclusions: Do not use this transport guideline to determine laboratory containment, biosafety levels, or clinical-waste classification or management.
Do not represent this guidance or review as an approval, compliance determination, export permission, or authorization to ship a specific material.
Do not treat statements in this Tier 2 technical guideline as Malaysian law or as an LMO regulatory determination.
Do not infer project-specific facts that were not provided and reviewed.
Do not treat a UN number, proper shipping name, or packing instruction mention as a determination that a specific shipment is classified, compliant, or approved.
findings: PDF page 11 states the guideline's purpose and coverage for clinical specimens and infectious substances within the country and abroad.
PDF page 17 requires classification according to Appendix 1 before determining appropriate packaging and describes basic triple packaging and Category A/B additional requirements.
PDF page 32 opens the marking and labelling section and states what marking and labelling must convey.
The table of contents on PDF page 9 lists dedicated PACKAGING and MARKING & LABELLING sections.
limitations: The guideline is a transport packaging and documentation guideline, not a laboratory containment or waste-management guideline.
The classification described is a transport classification; it is not a risk group or biosafety-level determination.
Sender duties such as confirming export legality with national authorities are sender responsibilities and do not establish general export permission.

atomic_propositions: The basic triple packaging system consists of three layers: a primary receptacle, a secondary receptacle to enclose and protect the primary receptacle, and a third outer layer of packaging.

An infectious substance can be classified into two transport categories; Category A covers substances that, when exposure occurs, could cause permanent disability, or life-threatening or fatal illness in otherwise healthy humans or animals.
Infectious substances are subclassified as Category B when they contain biological agents capable of causing infection in humans or animals but do not meet the Category A criteria.
The guideline assigns Packing Instruction P620 to Category A infectious substances and describes the packaging requirements P620 sets for Category A.

The guideline assigns Packing Instruction P650 to Category B infectious substances assigned to UN 3373 and describes P650 as a more detailed set of triple packaging requirements than the basic system.
exclusions: Do not use this transport guideline to determine laboratory containment, biosafety levels, or clinical-waste classification or management.
Do not represent this guidance or review as an approval, compliance determination, export permission, or authorization to ship a specific material.
Do not treat statements in this Tier 2 technical guideline as Malaysian law or as an LMO regulatory determination.
Do not infer project-specific facts that were not provided and reviewed.
Do not treat a UN number, proper shipping name, or packing instruction mention as a determination that a specific shipment is classified, compliant, or approved.
findings: PDF page 18 defines the basic triple packaging system as three layers.
PDF pages 22 and 26 define the Category A and Category B transport classifications.
PDF page 17 maps P620 to Category A and P650 to Category B assigned to UN 3373, and notes additional dry-ice requirements under PI 954.
PDF pages 24 and 26 present the P620 and P650 packing-instruction sections.
limitations: Category A and Category B here are transport classifications and must not be treated as risk groups or biosafety levels.
The P620 passage references packaging “approval” in the UN model-regulation sense; it does not establish that any specific shipment, facility, or activity is approved.
The dry-ice coolant reference (PI 954) is noted but was not separately propositioned.

atomic_propositions: The guideline's stated purpose is to ensure safe and secure packaging and transportation of clinical specimens and infectious substances within the country and abroad.
The guideline states that it does not describe the packaging and transportation of blood products, stem cell products, clinical waste and chemical waste.
exclusions: Do not use this transport guideline to determine laboratory containment, biosafety levels, or clinical-waste classification or management.
Do not represent this guidance or review as an approval, compliance determination, export permission, or authorization to ship a specific material.
Do not treat statements in this Tier 2 technical guideline as Malaysian law or as an LMO regulatory determination.
Do not infer project-specific facts that were not provided and reviewed.
Do not treat a UN number, proper shipping name, or packing instruction mention as a determination that a specific shipment is classified, compliant, or approved.
findings: PDF page 11 contains the guideline's own scope and exclusion statement.

PDF page 26 mentions “Clinical waste, unspecified, NOS” only as one possible UN 3291 proper shipping name for Category B infectious clinical or medical waste; that shipping-name mention does not bring general clinical-waste management within the guideline's described scope.
The historical editorial phrase “does not serve as the clinical-waste guideline” was not retained as a source proposition; the retained proposition uses the guideline's own wording.
limitations: The “does not describe” statement is the guideline's own scope statement and was not strengthened into a broader categorical or legal exclusion.
The guideline does not establish laboratory containment or waste-classification requirements.
Infectious clinical or medical waste assigned to Category B under UN 3291 remains subject to the transport provisions the guideline quotes.
